title: fix(app-shell,i18n): a signed-in user's language has one source of truth, sys_user.locale (objectui#10059)
body:
Fixes #10059

Clause-②: no

Executes ruling batch #193 item 5 letter C on objectui#10051 (maintainer 「其他同意」). Both halves land here, because either alone is a transitional half-state — the seed alone leaves the globe writing a value the next boot overrides, the write alone leaves the two controls agreeing only until a reload.

## What was wrong

One word 「语言」 named two settings. The profile page's language card writes the server column `sys_user.locale` (the column objectstack#14787 made writable, first written by objectui#7501). The console's globe menu switched a device-local UI language held in `@object-ui/i18n`'s `localStorage` slot. Neither writer could see the other, so a user who chose 日本語 on their profile went on reading an English console, with no refusal and no notice.

## What makes the divergence impossible now, not merely unlikely

For a signed-in user `sys_user.locale` is the only decider, and that is a property of the wiring rather than of anybody's discipline:

1. **One writer path.** The globe now writes the column, through the same adapter and the same object/field the profile card already used. There is no second place a language can be stored for a signed-in user.
2. **One reader, on the invalidation bus.** `useSignedInUserLocale` is mounted once in the console shell, beside `useMutationInvalidationBridge`. It reads the column on mount and again on every `sys_user` mutation that bus reports — and every adapter write reaches that bus, including the profile card's own save. So changing the language in either place changes it in both, in the same session, with no reload. That is the card's "changing either changes both", delivered without touching the profile page.
3. **The device value is demoted to a CACHE — kept, not removed and not ignored.** It still decides before sign-in and for the first paint of a boot, because the column cannot be read synchronously. It is overwritten by the column as soon as the row is read, so a stale device value has a bounded life of one round trip rather than a session or a device.

The write path applies the switch locally FIRST and then stores it, so a failed write leaves the switch standing and says so out loud (a `toast.error` carrying the server's own message), and the next successful read takes the UI back to what the column says. Never a silent no-op.

### The residue, stated rather than left to be found

The first paint of a boot renders from the device cache. A value changed on another device therefore shows for the length of one row read and is then replaced. That is the same stale-while-revalidate posture the tenant seed already ships with, and ending it would mean a blocking row read before `createRoot().render()` — which objectstack#5419 ruling point 3 already refused for the seed. It is named in the module docblock, not hidden.

⚠️ One earlier ruling is in tension and the newer one wins: objectstack#5419 point 3 says a late live language switch is worse than a flash, for an unauthenticated tenant seed on a first visit. This card's acceptance pin requires exactly such a late switch for a signed-in user whose device cache disagrees with their column ("sign in with server `ja` on a device cached `en` ⇒ UI `ja`"), so the signed-in path does it and the anonymous path is untouched.

## What a signed-out visitor sees — unchanged

Nothing here applies to them. With no `sys_user` row there is nothing to read and nothing to write: the reader does not fetch, the globe performs the local switch and returns, no request is attempted and no error is ever shown. Their language still comes from the device slot, then the tenant seed, then the browser, then `en` — the chain `@object-ui/i18n` already adjudicates. Signing out leaves the UI on the language it was showing, which is that slot's value, exactly as a globe switch has always left it.

## Where each half actually lives, and a correction to the card

The card assigns half 1 (seed precedence) to `packages/i18n`. Measured against the tree, it cannot live there and the reason is structural, so this PR places it one layer out and says so rather than splitting the difference:

- Reading `sys_user.locale` needs an authenticated data adapter. `@object-ui/i18n` is a renderer package that deliberately takes no such dependency — it owns policy, the host owns transport, which is the split `loadLanguage` / `loadLocales` / the tenant seed already follow. So the host applies the column through the ordinary `changeLanguage`, and `packages/i18n` changes here are prose only: its docblocks now state that a signed-in user's language is not one of the tiers its chain adjudicates, instead of the old claim that the device choice "outranks everything".
- ⛔ The obvious shortcut — promote the existing tenant-seed slot above the device choice — was rejected on measurement, not taste. That slot caches `GET /auth/me/localization`, whose `locale` is the user's own `sys_user.locale` **when set**, then the request's `Accept-Language`, then the deployment default (`@objectstack/spec`'s `SessionUser.language` retirement note states that cascade). The endpoint cannot say which rung answered, so promoting it would override the device choice of every signed-in user who has NO column value with a browser or deployment default — a silent regression for exactly the users who had used the globe before this change. The `sys_user` row read distinguishes set from unset, which is why it is the instrument.

An unset column therefore states nothing and changes nothing: the device value keeps deciding, and the user's first globe switch writes the column and ends that state for good.

## Acceptance

- `Clause-②: no` is copied from the claim comment, and the diff agrees with it: no new published export, no new key, no widened acceptance set. The new module is internal to `@object-ui/app-shell` and is not re-exported from its entry (`exports` names only the package root). ⚠️ The card's body predicts `yes` ("a behaviour change on the published app-shell"); the declared criterion is whether the change relaxes an acceptance set or widens the published surface, and a behaviour change alone is neither. Flagged for the seat rather than revised here.
- ⛔ No locale pack was touched — objectui#10172 holds `packages/i18n/src/locales/` and is unmerged. The failure toast reuses the existing `form.saveError` key, so no pack needed a new entry.
- ⛔ No rename of the profile option, and the objectui#7501 profile-page copy is untouched.
- Notifications keep reading `sys_user.locale`; nothing on that path moved.
- Changeset: `@object-ui/app-shell` minor, `@object-ui/i18n` patch. ⛔ Not `major`.

## Tests, and the ablation that proves they can fail

`pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/userLocale-10059.test.tsx` — 10 passed. `LocaleSwitcher.persistence`, `LocaleSwitcher.appLocales` and `studio-locale.i18n` — 15 passed, unchanged. `type-check` on both packages — clean, after building the dependency closure.

Each pin was ablated on disk through `ablation-replace`, which refuses an anchor that does not hit and verifies the mutation and the restore against the file's blob hash rather than an exit code. The tests import the mutated module by relative path, so they resolve SOURCE — there is no `dist/` in the resolution path and no build between mutate and run.

| ablation (anchor count 1 to 0, blob moves) | red |
| --- | --- |
| the globe no longer writes the column | "stores the switch on the server and shows it"; "reports a failed write loudly and leaves the switch standing" |
| the column is read and never applied | "seeds the UI from the column, over a device value that says otherwise"; "follows the column when the profile page writes it, with no reload"; and the read-back leg |
| successful reads are deduplicated by value | "reports a failed write loudly and leaves the switch standing" — its "until the next successful read" leg only |

The third arm is the one that keeps the per-read sequence honest: with the reads deduplicated the column stops re-asserting itself after a write that failed, and nothing else in the file notices.

## Gates run locally

`check-changeset-presence` 0 · `check-i18n-call-site-keys` 0 · `check-i18n-en-drift` 0 · `check-i18n-dead-keys` 0 · `check-control-bytes` 0 · `check-test-path-roots` 0 · `check-vi-mock-inherit` 0 · `check-vi-mock-specifiers` 0 · `check-vi-mock-override-shape` 0 · `eslint` on the changed files 0 (warnings only; the `ref.current` assignment during render matches this package's existing idiom in `AdapterProvider`).

## Acceptance notes

- The profile card's own description still says the interface language "is chosen separately, from the globe menu". After this change that sentence is false — the two are one setting. ⛔ Not repaired here: the ruling freezes the objectui#7501 copy and refused route D. Reported to the dispatching seat as a follow-up rather than filed from this branch.
- A deployment whose field-level security denies writing `sys_user.locale` now shows the failure toast on every globe switch. Deliberate: the alternative is a silent local-only switch, which is the divergence this card ends. The profile card asks `checkField` before rendering an editable control; the globe does not, because a menu that hides the language list on a permission answer is worse than a switch that tells the truth.
